question: What is the primary purpose of a referral system in community health?

options.A: To transfer administrative duties to community health workers
options.B: To reduce the total number of patients visiting clinics
options.C: To connect patients to the appropriate level of specialized care
options.D: To generate revenue for tertiary medical centers

explanation: A referral system ensures patients move seamlessly from primary facilities to higher tiers when their medical needs exceed local capabilities. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h1)

question: Why is an effective referral network particularly vital in resource-limited regions?

options.A: It prevents tertiary hospitals from becoming overwhelmed with minor cases
options.B: It eliminates the need for primary health care centers entirely
options.C: It guarantees free medical treatment at all levels of the health system
options.D: It replaces the need for community health education programs

explanation: Directing only complex cases upward keeps tertiary centers focused on specialized care while primary centers manage routine health needs. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h1)

question: What core element must accompany every patient being transferred to a higher health facility?

options.C: A personal letter from the village head
options.D: An advance booking for major surgery

explanation: A written referral note provides receiving clinicians with vital patient history, baseline vitals, and treatments already administered. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h2)

question: Why is two-way communication considered essential in a referral network?

options.A: It ensures feedback reaches the original clinic to complete the patient's care cycle
options.B: It forces tertiary doctors to visit community health posts regularly
options.C: It stops patients from changing their minds during transit
options.D: It allows the receiving facility to bill the primary center directly

explanation: Counter-referrals and communication back to the originating facility allow community health nurses to provide effective post-discharge follow-up care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h2)

question: Which tier of the Nigerian health system is primarily managed by the Local Government Authority?
explanation: Primary health care facilities, including health posts and PHCs, are administered at the local government level to ensure grassroot accessibility. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h3)

question: A patient requiring complex neurosurgery would most appropriately be sent to which facility tier?
explanation: Tertiary institutions like teaching hospitals possess the specialized surgical teams and advanced technology required for complex neurosurgical procedures. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h3)

question: Which of the following conditions is an absolute indication for immediate obstetric referral?
explanation: Obstructed labor poses an immediate life-threatening risk of uterine rupture and fetal distress, requiring emergency surgical intervention at a higher facility. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h4)

question: A six-month-old infant is brought to a primary health post with lethargy, inability to breastfeed, and sunken eyes. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Prescribe multivitamin drops and discharge the child
options.B: Reassure the mother and advise home fluid therapy only
options.C: Initiate immediate emergency referral to a higher facility
options.D: Schedule a follow-up appointment for the following week

explanation: Lethargy and inability to feed in an infant with signs of dehydration indicate severe illness requiring immediate facility-based stabilization and management. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h4)

question: What is the very first clinical priority before dispatching an unstable patient on referral?

options.A: Notifying the local print media of the transfer
options.B: Stabilizing the patient's immediate physiological condition
options.C: Completing the billing and insurance paperwork
options.D: Waiting for family members to raise transport funds

explanation: Emergency stabilization measures such as securing intravenous lines and airways must take precedence to keep the patient alive during transit. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h5)

question: Why should an unstable patient be accompanied by a trained health worker during transit?

options.A: To collect user fees on behalf of the referring clinic
options.B: To negotiate toll gates and fast-track road transport
options.C: To drive the ambulance in case the driver gets tired
options.D: To monitor vital signs and manage sudden clinical deterioration

explanation: An accompanying nurse or midwife can provide continuous observation and emergency interventions while the vehicle is in motion. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h5)

question: Which responsibility is a core duty of the community health nurse during a referral?

options.A: Financing the patient's hospital bill at the tertiary center
options.B: Performing major specialized surgery at the primary clinic
options.C: Manufacturing the medications prescribed by the specialist
options.D: Preparing the patient and family psychologically for the transfer

explanation: Counseling and preparing patients help reduce anxiety and build trust in the referral facility, improving adherence to the transfer plan. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h6)

question: How do community health nurses assist in overcoming transport barriers in rural areas?

options.A: By converting the health post into an emergency operating theater
options.B: By advising patients to walk to the nearest city hospital
options.C: By purchasing personal vehicles to transport all clinic patients
options.D: By collaborating with local transport groups and community emergency schemes

explanation: Engaging local transport stakeholders creates reliable community-based mobilization systems to move patients when emergencies strike. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h6)

question: What is a major financial barrier that prevents rural patients from accepting referrals?

options.A: Compulsory insurance registration for outpatient visits
options.B: Excessive charges for obtaining community health cards
options.C: High out-of-pocket costs for transport and hospital fees
options.D: Mandatory taxation levied on all community clinics

explanation: The financial burden of transport and perceived treatment costs at higher facilities causes dangerous delays in seeking care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h7)

question: Which factor is NOT a typical operational bottleneck in community-level referral systems?

options.A: Guaranteed availability of free fuel in all primary ambulances
options.B: Cultural preference for traditional healers during obstetric crises
options.C: Communication gaps between primary clinics and tertiary hospitals
options.D: Poor road infrastructure connecting rural areas to cities

explanation: Reliable fuel availability is an ideal resource, whereas fuel shortages and logistical failures are actual barriers in community settings. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h7)

question: What is a counter-referral in community health practice?

options.A: Transferring a nurse from a rural post to an urban teaching hospital
options.B: Sending a stabilized patient back from a higher facility to the primary health center
options.C: Referring a patient to a traditional healer after medical treatment
options.D: Rejecting a patient admission due to a lack of available hospital beds

explanation: A counter-referral returns the patient to the community level for continued care and monitoring once acute specialist intervention concludes. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h8)

question: Why is post-discharge home visitation by the community health nurse vital after a counter-referral?

options.A: To write a new medical diagnosis for the patient's health record
options.B: To evaluate the home environment and support ongoing recovery compliance
options.C: To collect payment for the specialized surgery performed downtown
options.D: To transport other sick family members back to the tertiary hospital

explanation: Home visits enable the nurse to observe recovery conditions firsthand, check medication adherence, and provide localized support. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h8)
